reasons.D: Closest to the passage's assertive, epigrammatic wit ("heroic on Monday and shabby on Tuesday, and both from the purest motives"); varied lengths, semicolon joins, a single dash, and a short worldly closing turn match the author's confident, slightly ironic stance.
reasons.A: Right period diction and semicolon-balanced sentences, but more hedged and genteel ("I venture to say", "I fancy", "it must be admitted") than the passage's crisper assertions; less epigrammatic bite.
reasons.B: Chatty, clubbable register ("the other fellow", "earns its keep", parenthetical aside) and many short conversational sentences; lighter and cosier than the author's pointed, aphoristic manner.
reasons.C: Plain modern expository prose with even sentence lengths, list-like clauses and a summarising close; lacks the irony, wit and period flavour of the passage.
